criterion.candidates: the 1049 blocks `tools/script_profile.py` admits (M146): among the 8091 {offset,size} entries at cart 0x0c8624 + 0x28, a member that inflates, is at least 8 B, whose head is a u16 record table of at least two entries, and whose records decode to at least MIN_COMMANDS (4) known commands. Reproduced here by importing script_profile.walk_block and applying that test unchanged; fixtures/scd/profile.json is the citation, and --check asserts the reproduction (1049 scripts, 5111 records, 102673 walker commands).

categories.code_referenced: the id is materialised as a constant into an argument register of a call to the cartridge's file-table accessor, derived from file_table.py's five sound-family ids plus an 8-byte stride in the accessor's body. The instruction address is recorded.
categories.heuristic_only: the block decodes to >= 4 instructions and no search found a reference to it.
categories.not_a_script: the M213 decoder yields fewer than 4 instructions for the whole block, or refuses at its first byte; first_refusal carries the decoder's own message.
categories.room_table: the file id is an entry of DAT_80131fa8, the table the room loader reads; the artefact lists the room indices that name it.
categories.script_referenced: a script-table reference from a block already classified 1 or 2. Empty by mechanism: the index is u8 into the block's own u16[] record table.

criterion.counts: records = u16 record-table entries per block (the admitting criterion's own enumeration, so the total is the profile's 5111). commands = instructions the M213 decoder actually decoded, fewer than the linear walker's 102673 because every record is bounded by its own end and a refusal ends a record instead of guessing past it.
criterion.order_rule: the first category whose evidence holds wins, in the order above. A block named by the room table is therefore room_table even if the decoder then refuses part of it; that refusal is still recorded in its first_refusal.

profile.note: the claim M156/M157 refuted as a population; this artefact classifies it

notes: heuristic_only is not 'not used'; it is 'no reference found yet'. The three searches are the room table (256 entries), a constant argument to a derived file-table accessor, and the script-table operands this VM has. A reference through a data table this tool does not model lands outside all three and still reads heuristic_only.

The accessor set is derived, not hardcoded: 0x80004930 (anchors [1979, 1983], stride 0x80004938), 0x80004c9c (anchors [1980, 1981, 1982], stride 0x80004ca8), 0x80004cfc (anchors [1980, 1981, 1982], stride 0x80004d3c). Each was accepted because a call passes it one of the five sound-family ids file_table.py established AND its body contains the 8-byte stride that indexes a {offset,size} entry. Corroboration, not part of the test: the init behind the first accessor (0x80004954) reads cart record 0x43 and stores count*8 + 0x28 into the global that accessor loads as its table base - this population's own table. A fourth accessor that no anchor id reaches would not be recognised.

A bare 'the value appears as a constant in code' scan was run and REFUSED as evidence: 18 of the 1049 have such an immediate, in 41 instruction(s), and their contexts are coordinates, struct fields, draw-call arguments or RSP microcode data - 1900 is stored by `sh v0,368(s0)` beside 950 and 3000 at 0x801621e4 (and 1900 is a room id, so this coincidence would have been invisible), 7120 and 7096 are coordinates loaded into a0 at 0x8016cdb0 and 0x80166a84 beside stack arrays of positions, 7520 is added to a struct pointer as a byte offset at 0x8016228c, and 3512/3552 sit in a stage-2 region whose `jal` targets are 0x84xxxxxx - RSP instruction memory, not MIPS code. Their ids and counts are in refused.code_referenced_by_bare_immediate, and --check asserts the anchor filters.

4 of the 1049 reach some call's argument register, across 7 call site(s): 3584 -> 0x80167bd8 from ovl_00a733e@0x80162660; 3585 -> 0x801667c0 from ovl_00ae24a@0x80165100; 7000 -> 0x80057718 from ovl_0014420@0x80055bb8; 7000 -> 0x80036ea0 from ovl_008900e@0x80162938; 7000 -> 0x80036ea0 from ovl_008e046@0x80162938; 7000 -> 0x80037780 from ovl_007fc12@0x80166bac; 7120 -> 0x80037780 from ovl_007fc12@0x8016cdb0. None reaches an accessor, so each stays heuristic_only with the call recorded here rather than promoted on an adjacency.

The room table names 147 distinct ids and 50 of them are among the 1049. The rest cannot appear here at all: M158 read 48 as the 32-byte `01 41` container family, 43 as other resources and 6 as not zlib — which is why the room-script population is 50 and not 147.

totals.commands is the M213 decoder's count over the same 5111 records; it is smaller than the profile's 102673 because the decoder bounds every record by its own end and stops at a refusal, where the linear walker keeps advancing through the block. The difference is the decoder's honesty, itemised per block in first_refusal and in decoder.refusals.

script_referenced is an empty category, not an unfilled one: no search result could have put a block there, because the index is a u8 into the block's own u16[] record table (`--check` asserts exactly that). The measurement a looser rule would have produced is in `refused`, so the empty category is reviewable rather than merely empty.
